diseases.name: Citrus Canker
diseases.description: A bacterial disease of citrus leaves, twigs and fruit that leaves raised, corky spots.
diseases.causes: Wind-driven rain spreads the bacteria; they enter through pores and wounds, including citrus leafminer tunnels.
symptoms: Raised, corky tan-brown spots on both sides of the leaf
A water-soaked margin and yellow halo round each spot
Similar scabby spots on fruit and twigs
diseases.effect: Spotted leaves and fruit drop early; marked fruit cannot be sold fresh.
diseases.untreated: Heavy infection defoliates trees and causes large fruit losses; the disease is regulated in many countries.

steps.title: Report it where required
steps.instruction: Check whether citrus canker must be reported to the plant-health service in your area.
steps.rationale: It is a regulated quarantine disease in many places.

steps.title: Prune out infected shoots in dry weather
steps.instruction: Remove spotted twigs and leaves and disinfect the tools.
steps.rationale: Lowers the bacteria washed onto new growth.

steps.title: Protect new growth with copper
steps.instruction: Spray a registered copper product on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Copper protects new flushes and young fruit.

prevention.title: Control citrus leafminer
prevention.detail: Its tunnels let the bacteria in.

prevention.title: Disinfect tools and equipment
prevention.detail: Bacteria travel between trees on them.

lifecycle: Bacteria survive in spots on leaves, twigs and fruit.
Wind-driven rain splashes them onto new growth.
They enter through pores and wounds.
Raised corky spots with yellow halos form.
